correctness.rationale: At each n aperiodicity provides a right-special factor; complement closure gives its distinct complementary right-special factor, so each p(n+1)-p(n)>=2 and p(n)>=2n. Bitwise complement permutes G-orbit classes in free two-cycles at odd n because no odd-length binary word can share its Hamming weight with its complement. Thus all G-complexities are even and p_ab+1 is odd and <=n+2<=2n<=p at every odd n>=3. At n<=2 no gaps can occur for any binary word. Direct S3 subgroup enumeration reproduces {2:2,4:3,6:1} for Thue--Morse. Full infinite proof independent of finite program.

value.rationale: The theorem settles failure of a recently introduced universal group-complexity property uniformly across the natural infinite class of all aperiodic binary languages invariant under alphabet complement, and at each odd factor length, not merely for a particular automatic word. The sharp universal first-obstruction length n=3, simultaneous lower factor-growth bound p(n)>=2n, and nonattainment of a concrete in-range integer organize this whole class structurally. The method extends a credited individual Thue--Morse parity observation; the main mathematical value is the general no-go classification and sharp onset, not isolated computation.
